sources.versionScope: Google SRE book chapter 21, resource limits and Deciding to Retry sections inspected 2026-10-17
sources.notes: Adopt bounded work and retry ownership. Google topology and numerical thresholds are examples, not mandatory architecture.

sources.versionScope: IEEE Computer Society SWEBOK landing page, including its v4.0a update notice, inspected 2026-10-17; full guide not inspected
sources.notes: Orientation and professional responsibility only; the landing page does not establish transaction, queue, or durability guarantees.

sources.versionScope: Google Site Reliability Engineering book as available 2026-09-04
sources.notes: Navigation for reliability topics only. Use the inspected chapter or actual adapter contract for behavioral claims.

sources.versionScope: Amazon Builders' Library article, request identity, atomic mutation, semantic equivalence, late requests, and changed intent sections inspected 2026-10-17
sources.notes: Adopt scoped caller intent, atomic effect and deduplication evidence, compatible retry results, and explicit retention. EC2 token lifetime is an example, not a universal expiry policy.

sources.versionScope: PostgreSQL 18 section 13.2, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable behavior inspected 2026-10-17
sources.notes: Adopt explicit isolation and full transaction retries after serialization failure. PostgreSQL behavior does not establish another engine's locking, isolation, or commit guarantees.

sources.versionScope: Microsoft Graph delta query overview, opaque state tokens, empty pages, replays, and synchronization reset sections inspected 2026-10-17
sources.notes: Adopt inspecting continuation, replay, and reset semantics. Graph entity IDs are not stable change IDs; its resource-specific token durations and status codes are not generic feed guarantees.

sources.versionScope: Azure Architecture Center Compensating Transaction pattern, concurrent work, resumable compensation, and irreversible steps inspected 2026-10-17
sources.notes: Adopt durable compensation progress and domain-specific recovery that preserves concurrent changes. Reject the introductory preference for eventual consistency as a universal rule and do not require Azure services or sagas.
